label: late encoding / <DEL> step, first-occurrence input, sequence starting with a/y/0/c/d/q/s/u
explanation: Fires only in the original-input phase from t>=4 (mostly t=5-9) and at the <DEL> step (52% of mass; 31% of DEL steps active). Never fires during copy phase (t>L) or at t<=2. 94% of mass is on first occurrences of the input token (repeated tokens rarely fire). Strongly modulated by the first original token: sequences starting with a, y, 0, c, d, q (and less s, u) fire at ~2.5x base rate and dominate the top activations (top examples nearly all start with a or d); the second token adds a weaker dependence, suggesting it reads a distributed hidden-state code of the sequence prefix. Inputs o, z, 2, 3 also raise the rate. Longer L gives more firing. Predicate captures ~61% of mass at ~0.57 precision on dev; the remainder looks like a distributed prefix-dependent code with no simple description.
